templates.name: Sun Chaser
templates.description: Catch sunshine and make a light shine.
steps: The circuit is already running: catch the sunshine.
Open Surroundings and move Sunshine down, then up.
Watch the LED change with the available energy.
templates.expected: Catch sunshine and make a light shine.
templates.variation: Change one control or connection, predict the result, then try it.

templates.name: Battery Team
templates.description: Two battery packs work together for a six-volt bulb.
steps: Follow the connection between the two battery packs.
Watch the six-volt bulb.
Select each battery to compare its voltage.
templates.expected: Two battery packs work together for a six-volt bulb.
templates.variation: Change one control or connection, predict the result, then try it.

templates.name: Rainbow Row
templates.description: Make three colours glow side by side.
steps: Find all three colours.
Turn on Dark Night to see their light spill.
Select each LED and compare the current.
templates.expected: Make three colours glow side by side.
templates.variation: Change one control or connection, predict the result, then try it.

templates.name: Firefly Jar
templates.description: Store a little energy and watch it fade into light.
steps: Hold the yellow button for two seconds.
Release the button and watch the little light fade.
The capacitor is giving back its stored energy.
templates.expected: Store a little energy and watch it fade into light.
templates.variation: Change one control or connection, predict the result, then try it.

templates.name: Reverse the Fan
templates.description: Change the connections to change the spin.
steps: Watch the fan.
Select the motor and choose Swap the two ends. Its blue snap paths stay in place.
Watch the motor slow down and turn the other way.
templates.expected: Change the connections to change the spin.
templates.variation: Change one control or connection, predict the result, then try it.

templates.name: Wind Makes Watts
templates.description: Wind turns a generator into a tiny power station.
steps: Watch the wind turn the fan.
Move Wind in Surroundings and watch the meter.
The moving motor is making electricity.
templates.expected: Wind turns a generator into a tiny power station.
templates.variation: Change one control or connection, predict the result, then try it.

templates.name: Tap a Secret
templates.description: Send a secret message with short and long flashes.
steps: Hold and release the yellow button.
Try three short flashes, then one long flash.
Ask someone to repeat your message.
templates.expected: Send a secret message with short and long flashes.
templates.variation: Change one control or connection, predict the result, then try it.

templates.name: Dimmer Detective
templates.description: Turn the yellow dial to change a light.
steps: Select the adjustable resistor.
Drag the yellow handle left or right.
A small change near the bright end makes a big difference.
templates.expected: Turn the yellow dial to change a light.
templates.variation: Change one control or connection, predict the result, then try it.

templates.name: One-Way Gate
templates.description: Discover which way a diode lets current flow.
steps: Watch current pass through the diode.
Select the diode and choose Swap the two ends. Its blue snap paths stay in place.
The one-way gate now stops the light.
templates.expected: Discover which way a diode lets current flow.
templates.variation: Change one control or connection, predict the result, then try it.

templates.name: Tiny Switch, Big Job
templates.description: A small button asks a transistor to run a motor.
steps: Hold the yellow button.
Watch the motor turn while the transistor carries its current.
Release the button to stop asking for power.
templates.expected: A small button asks a transistor to run a motor.
templates.variation: Change one control or connection, predict the result, then try it.

templates.name: Wire Flyover
templates.description: Let two paths cross while their plastic keeps them apart.
steps: Use Top view to find the crossing.
Use Exploded layers to see the gap between the paths.
Try the slide switch.
templates.expected: Let two paths cross while their plastic keeps them apart.
templates.variation: Change one control or connection, predict the result, then try it.

templates.name: Lighthouse Tower
templates.description: Stack connector pairs to lift a beacon above the board.
steps: Use Exploded layers to count the stacked connectors.
Return to normal view and watch the beacon.
Look at the beacon in Dark Night.
templates.expected: Stack connector pairs to lift a beacon above the board.
templates.variation: Change one control or connection, predict the result, then try it.

templates.name: Traffic-Light Dance
templates.description: An AVR follows your blocks to change three traffic lights.
steps: Watch the lights take turns.
Open Code and change one waiting time.
Send your blocks to the controller, and watch your new dance.
templates.expected: The controller changes electrical pins and the connected light responds.
templates.variation: Change one control or connection, predict the result, then try it.

templates.name: Dial-a-Glow
templates.description: A PIC reads a real button and dial, then drives its LED pin.
steps: Hold the yellow button.
Release it, move the dial, then hold the button again. Compare the glow.
Open Code to see how the input controls the output.
templates.expected: The controller changes electrical pins and the connected light responds.
templates.variation: Change one control or connection, predict the result, then try it.

templates.name: Gear Buddies
templates.description: Two supported gears turn together: one slower, one faster.

hardware.note: Elenco lists 1-inch GEAR1 and 1.75-inch GEAR2 parts. Their outer sizes inform these models; tooth counts (12/22), axle adapters, bearing stand and friction are estimates. Use compatible shafts and your kit’s actual tooth counts for a physical build; do not assume the stand is a supplied Snap Circuits part.

sources.title: Elenco parts catalogue: gears and geared motor

steps: Click the green slide switch to stop and start the gears.
Follow the white marks: the bigger gear turns slower and the other way.
Select the big gear and hold it still. The motor’s current rises. Release it again.
templates.expected: Two supported gears turn together: one slower, one faster.
templates.variation: Change one control or connection, predict the result, then try it.

templates.name: Relay Light Swap
templates.description: An electromagnet chooses between two lights on a separate battery.

hardware.note: S3 is a changeover relay: identify its coil, common, normally open and normally closed contacts from your manual. Use two separate 3 V supplies and a 100 Ω resistor for each LED. Our coil resistance, pickup threshold and snap layout are estimates, so this is a functional equivalent, not an exact S3 construction diagram.

sources.title: Elenco STEM: relay and separate coil/contact circuits

steps: Click the slide switch: green and red take turns.
The coil battery pulls a tiny switch inside the relay. The other battery powers the lights.
Hover over a blue connector or cable to follow its path. The two battery loops stay separate.
templates.expected: An electromagnet chooses between two lights on a separate battery.
templates.variation: Change one control or connection, predict the result, then try it.

templates.name: NPN Lantern
templates.description: A tiny base current opens the light’s path back to the battery.

hardware.note: Functional build with B1 (3 V), S1, Q2, R1 (100 Ω), R2 (1 kΩ), R4 (10 kΩ) and D1. Znatok counterparts are shown in Real-life labels. Match B/C/E by label, not by body orientation. Keep the external LED resistor; kit LEDs may also contain protection.

sources.title: Elenco: NPN and PNP parts and circuits

steps: Click the slide switch to turn the lantern off and on.
Find B, C and E on the NPN. The little base signal lets current return through C to E.
The 1 kΩ resistor limits base current; the 10 kΩ resistor makes sure the transistor turns off.
templates.expected: A tiny base current opens the light’s path back to the battery.
templates.variation: Change one control or connection, predict the result, then try it.

templates.name: PNP Lantern
templates.description: This transistor switches the light from the battery’s plus side.

hardware.note: Uses the same values as NPN Lantern, with Q1 (PNP). Its emitter goes to battery +. Follow the labelled terminals: exchanging NPN and PNP without rewiring does not work.

sources.title: Elenco: NPN and PNP parts and circuits

steps: Click the slide switch to turn the lantern off and on.
The emitter E is at battery +. A base path towards − turns this PNP on.
Compare with NPN Lantern: the transistor is on the other side of the light.
templates.expected: This transistor switches the light from the battery’s plus side.
templates.variation: Change one control or connection, predict the result, then try it.

templates.name: NPN + PNP Team
templates.description: The NPN asks the PNP to turn on a light. Follow the message!

hardware.note: Functional build with Q2 + Q1, a 3 V B1, S1, D1, one 100 Ω, two 1 kΩ and two 10 kΩ resistors. Some kits need extra resistors. Match B/C/E and use the terminal guide; this is an original circuit, not a numbered manufacturer project.

sources.title: Elenco: NPN and PNP parts and circuits

steps: Click the slide switch and watch the light.
Follow the NPN collector to the PNP base resistor: one transistor asks the other to switch.
Turn it off. Both 10 kΩ resistors help their transistors return to the off state.
templates.expected: The NPN asks the PNP to turn on a light. Follow the message!
templates.variation: Change one control or connection, predict the result, then try it.

templates.name: Filament Flash
templates.description: Find out why a small bulb cannot take a big electrical push.
steps: This is a virtual experiment. Never copy it with real parts.
Press Run and watch the condition and current readings.
Select the broken part, replace it, then try Guided mode.
templates.expected: The intended part fails and stays broken until you replace it.
templates.variation: Compare the same circuit in Guided mode: it pauses before damage.

templates.name: NPN Night Watch
templates.description: An automatic night light with just one NPN transistor.
steps: It starts at night. Watch your automatic night light.
Press Dark Night to swap between night and day. The light sensor changes the signal at B.
In daylight, the sensor carries the base signal away to −. At night, the resistor lets the NPN turn on.
templates.expected: Darkness turns the LED on; daylight turns it off.
templates.variation: In daylight, change Sunshine under Surroundings to explore the point where the LED changes.

sources.title: Elenco: Q2 NPN, Q1 PNP and component values

hardware.note: Original 3 V circuit using exactly one Q2 NPN and no opposite-type transistor or computer. Use RP, R4 (10 kΩ), R1 (100 Ω), S1 and D1. Follow B/C/E and the terminal guide. Kit values, sensor thresholds and timing vary; this is a functional circuit, not a copied manufacturer project or a verified physical layout.

templates.name: NPN Porch Timer
templates.description: A useful light that stays on briefly after you release the button. One NPN does the switching.
steps: Hold the yellow button for one or two seconds to fill the capacitor with energy.
Let go. The transistor keeps the light on while the capacitor’s signal slowly fades.
The capacitor keeps B above the emitter for a while, then the light goes out.
templates.expected: The LED stays lit briefly after release, then fades out. A longer button press stores more energy.
templates.variation: Compare a short press with a long press. Predict which gives the longer glow.

sources.title: Elenco: Q2 NPN, Q1 PNP and component values

hardware.note: Original 3 V circuit using exactly one Q2 NPN and no opposite-type transistor or computer. Use S2, C5 (470 µF), R2 (1 kΩ), R4 (10 kΩ), R3 (5.1 kΩ), R1 (100 Ω) and D1. Keep the capacitor’s + end at the higher voltage. Follow B/C/E and the terminal guide. Kit values, sensor thresholds and timing vary; this is a functional circuit, not a copied manufacturer project or a verified physical layout.

templates.name: NPN Desk Fan
templates.description: Use a small dial to control a fan through one NPN transistor.
steps: The fan starts running. Click the slide switch to stop and start it.
Select the dial and slide its handle. Compare a low setting near 0.05 with a setting near 0.6.
The dial sends a small signal to B. The NPN carries the motor current; the diode catches the motor’s switch-off pulse.
templates.expected: The dial changes the motor’s current and speed. The switch stops supplying energy and the fan coasts down.
templates.variation: Try turning the dial halfway, then almost all the way. Watch the motor’s current as well as its speed.

sources.title: Elenco: Q2 NPN, Q1 PNP and component values

hardware.note: Original 3 V circuit using exactly one Q2 NPN and no opposite-type transistor or computer. Use RV (50 kΩ), R2 (1 kΩ), R4 (10 kΩ), S1, M1 with fan, and D3. Check the diode band and motor current. Follow B/C/E and the terminal guide. Kit values, sensor thresholds and timing vary; this is a functional circuit, not a copied manufacturer project or a verified physical layout.

templates.name: PNP Sunrise Beacon
templates.description: A daylight signal with just one PNP transistor.
steps: Sunshine turns on the beacon. It could tell you when it is time to open the curtains.
Press Dark Night to swap between night and day. The light sensor changes the signal at B.
In daylight, the sensor pulls the base below the emitter at +. That turns the PNP on. Darkness lets it turn off.
templates.expected: Daylight turns the LED on; darkness turns it off.
templates.variation: In daylight, change Sunshine under Surroundings to explore the point where the LED changes.
